candidate_findings.title: Helper restart and failover lack a bounded lifecycle state machine
candidate_findings.gap: RM-020 names deterministic disposal, failed-teardown diagnostics, new helper identity, memory-pressure restart, and failover without defining the transitions connecting them.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Partial disposal, concurrent in-flight work, or repeated pressure can produce restart storms, duplicate or lost work, abandoned sessions, and helper identities whose ownership cannot be reconstructed.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The pressure metric, sampling window, thresholds, close ordering, close deadlines, partial-failure state, restart-versus-failover precedence, retry cap, old-to-new identity correlation, in-flight ownership transfer, and terminal or persisted outcome are unspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Runtime teardown deterministically closes DB handles, MCP sessions, terminal shells, temporary files, and subprocess groups, emits diagnostics for failed teardown, mints new helper identity after restart, and monitors long-lived helper memory pressure for controlled restart or failover.

candidate_findings.title: HTE tool-observation kill has an undefined race boundary
candidate_findings.gap: The first observed provider tool_use is terminal, but observation and termination are not defined for streamed, partial, malformed, duplicated, or replayed provider events.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A handler can dispatch or queue prohibited work before the kill becomes authoritative, while duplicate observations can create multiple terminal representations or leak tool arguments into durable metadata.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Event framing, the exact observation point, cancellation order relative to any dispatcher, idempotency under replay, provider-process teardown, queued-handler disposition, tool-argument redaction, and atomic consistency between the terminal done event and run.completed metadata are unspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: The first provider-originated tool_use observed during HTE terminates the run immediately with stop_reason kill.hte_tool_observed in the terminal normalized done event and persisted run.completed metadata.

candidate_findings.title: DAE kill counters omit thresholds and concurrency scope
candidate_findings.gap: RM-022 defines qualifying and excluded events but never states the count that triggers kill.shell_failure or kill.write_thrash.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can choose incompatible kill thresholds, and restarts or concurrent writers can evade or spuriously amplify counting.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Numeric thresholds, the exact shell-fingerprint and jail-path normalization algorithms, counter ownership scope, ordering for concurrent events, persistence across helper or process restart, boundary-time semantics for the sliding window, and the authoritative reset event are unspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: DAE-specific kill counting treats shell_failure as actual executed canonical shell invocation failures for one normalized fingerprint, excludes denials and UI-only terminal actions, resets on success or replacement, and treats write_thrash as qualifying content-changing writes to one normalized jail path in a sliding 10-minute window.

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A scan failure following cancellation, crash, timeout, budget exhaustion, or another kill can replace the causal outcome and present misleading operational or GUI truth.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Outcome-precedence rules, preservation of the pre-scan outcome and stop reason, aggregation when multiple scans fail, scan timeout and cancellation behavior, scan ordering, and redaction and size limits for persisted scan details are unspecified.
